references.text: Jethro advised Moses to appoint leaders over the people, and Moses followed this advice. This is the background for the arrangement that Moses refers to in Deuteronomy.
Moses listened to his father-in-law's counsel and chose capable men from all Israel as leaders. The positive response of the people in Deuteronomy reflects this earlier event.
The Lord commanded Moses to gather seventy of Israel's elders to share the leadership responsibility. This shows a similar arrangement of delegated leadership that the people approved.
The preceding verse where Moses asks the people to choose wise and experienced men as leaders, which the people then respond to positively.
The following verse describes how Moses actually appointed the leaders after the people had approved the proposal.
